title: Mandela Wears the Springbok Jersey
text:
In 1995, a year after the end of apartheid, South Africa hosted the Rugby World Cup. Rugby was the sport of the white Afrikaner minority, and the green Springbok jersey was, for many black South Africans, a symbol of the old regime. Some in the African National Congress wanted the Springbok name and emblem dropped.

Nelson Mandela, now president, took the opposite view. He argued for keeping the name, met the team, and built a relationship with its captain, Francois Pienaar. The squad learned to sing Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika, which now stood beside the old anthem Die Stem as one of the country's two national anthems.

On June 24, 1995, South Africa played New Zealand in the final at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, before a mostly white crowd. Mandela walked onto the field wearing a Springbok jersey and cap, with Pienaar's number 6 on the back. The crowd began chanting his name.

South Africa won 15 to 12 in extra time. Mandela handed the trophy to Pienaar, who said afterward that the team had not had the support of 63,000 South Africans but of 43 million.
lesson: Reaching out to the people who fear you, through what they care about, can do more to build unity than any speech.
source: Contemporary press reports; John Carlin, Playing the Enemy (2008)
place: Ellis Park Stadium, Johannesburg, South Africa
